channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Turkmenistan prioritizes TAPI pipeline and Caspian Sea route for gas exports
item.description: Turkmenistan is accelerating efforts to diversify its natural gas exports. The first section of the TAPI pipeline to Herat is expected by end-2026. The trans-Caspian pipeline is now a priority, as China currently takes most Turkmen gas. Turkmenistan signed a letter of intent for gas distribution in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vice-President Chairs Meeting on Implementing President's Initiatives
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice-President Yerlan Karin chaired a meeting in Akorda focused on strengthening interethnic harmony and implementing initiatives from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's first People's Council session. The meeting involved heads of various ministries and discussed advancing the president's key positions and ensuring close monitoring of his directives. Constitutional values of interethnic and interfaith accord were highlighted as foundational for stable state development.

item.title: Strengthening Interethnic Accord Discussed at Kazakhstan's Akorda
item.description: Kazakhstan's Akorda hosted a meeting chaired by Vice-President Yerlan Karin to discuss strengthening interethnic harmony and implementing President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives from the first session of the People's Council. Participants included heads of key ministries and the General Prosecutor's Office. The meeting emphasized the importance of constitutional values of interethnic and interfaith accord as a foundation for the nation's stable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Sign Agreement Establishing Higher Council for Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan have signed an agreement to establish a Higher Council for Strategic Partnership. The agreement aims to deepen political dialogue and expand practical cooperation in priority areas, including trade, economy, industry, energy, transport, and agriculture.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes New Entry Requirements for Travelers to Egypt
item.description: Starting November 1, Uzbekistan citizens will need to obtain entry visas for Egypt in advance from Egyptian diplomatic missions. Tourist trips must be organized through authorized tour operators. Travelers under 40 require pre-approved visas and must be accompanied by close family members, with a minimum of $5,000 in cash. Independent travelers over 40 need at least $3,000.

item.title: Almaty City Administration Addresses Concerns Over Hazardous Wheelchair Ramps
item.description: The Almaty city administration has responded to resident complaints about hazardous wheelchair ramps in the reconstructed Republic Square. Some ramps are reportedly damaged, and their usability for people with limited mobility is questioned, with one user noting stairs at the end of a ramp. The administration acknowledges the issue and plans to repair and improve the ramps as part of ongoing landscaping work.

item.title: Angren Hydroelectric Power Plant Updated for Safety and Water Quality
item.description: The Angren Reservoir and HPP in Uzbekistan have been updated with European and Chinese technologies to ensure safe operation and water quality. Director Rakhmanov stated that 10 previously non-operational wells were repaired and equipped with modern sensors. Water level and condition monitoring is now online, replacing manual checks, providing real-time data on dam stability and water flow.

item.title: Afghanistan's UN Representative Urges Taliban to End Gender Apartheid
item.description: Naseer Ahmad Faiq, Afghanistan's acting UN representative, called on the Taliban to end gender apartheid and discriminatory decrees against women and girls. He stated that these policies contradict Islamic teachings and Afghan culture, depriving women and girls of basic rights and opportunities.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts International Seminar on Greening Aviation
item.description: Tashkent is hosting an international seminar organized by ICAO and ACI EUROPE, with support from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport, focusing on making air travel more environmentally friendly. The event brings together aviation industry stakeholders to discuss sustainable development models for airport infrastructure.

item.title: Business Manager of Karachaganak Support Service Sentenced to 10 Years for Embezzling $2.2 Million
item.description: A court in Uralsk has sentenced Barlyk Mendygaziyev, business manager of Karachaganak Support Service (KSS), to 10 years in prison for embezzling $2.2 million. He defrauded the company by transferring funds to a US-based firm he controlled under the guise of purchasing equipment.

item.title: Russian religious figure opposing Ukraine war sentenced to 4 years in Almaty
item.description: A religious figure from Russia, known for opposing the war in Ukraine, has been sentenced to four years in prison in Almaty. Additionally, an investigation reveals the son-in-law of the President of Uzbekistan has secretly obtained UAE citizenship. A Dutch company developed software for easy control of multiple drones from one system.

item.title: Kazakhstan's interfaith harmony discussed at OSCE conference in Warsaw
item.description: Kazakhstan's model of interfaith dialogue and cooperation was presented at the OSCE Human Dimension Conference in Warsaw. Representatives highlighted how daily interaction and mutual understanding strengthen religious harmony. A club of religious associations, active since 2021, includes 14 confessions working to foster peaceful coexistence while respecting differences.

item.title: UNICEF reports positive impact of water and health investments in Parwan Province, Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF representative Tajudeen Oyewale stated that investments in water and health sectors in Parwan Province have yielded positive results. UNICEF has expanded solar-powered water systems and sanitation services in schools, health centers, and communities, improving access to clean water. No water-related diseases have been reported this year in the covered areas.

item.title: One of Three Missing Kazakh Women in Nepal Found Alive, MFA Reports
item.description: The Kazakh Foreign Ministry in Astana announced that one of three Kazakh citizens initially reported missing after a natural disaster in Nepal in late August has been found alive. The ministry confirmed contact has been established with her, and she had canceled her trip to the disaster zone. The whereabouts of two other Kazakh women remain unknown, with relatives undergoing identification procedures.

item.title: Kazakh National Missing in Nepal Found and Returned Home, MFA Reports
item.description: A Kazakh national, initially reported missing after a natural disaster in Nepal, has been located and returned to Kazakhstan. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed contact was made with one of three missing tourists. Efforts continue to locate the other two, with relatives providing biological samples for DNA analysis.

item.title: Pavlodar Environmental Prosecutor's Office Overturns Fines Against 34 Businesses
item.description: The Pavlodar environmental prosecutor's office has overturned administrative offense rulings against 34 businesses, including one investor. The rulings were issued by the ecology department without proper verification. An official responsible has been fined, and the entrepreneurs were freed from unlawful administrative responsibility.

item.title: Uzbek President proposes unified Central Asian computing infrastructure
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed creating a common computing infrastructure for Central Asian nations during a summit in Avaza, Turkmenistan. This network of interconnected national data centers would enable efficient use of computing power and development of digital products and AI projects.

item.title: Kazakh MFA provides update on citizens missing after Nepal and Tibet disaster
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is monitoring the situation of citizens affected by natural disasters in Nepal and Tibet. Search operations have concluded in Nepal, with recovery efforts underway. In Tibet, searches continue, and identification processes are ongoing for discovered remains.

item.title: Kazakhstan allocates nearly one billion tenge for Balkhash Airport renovation
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov inspected the modernization of Balkhash city's social and transport infrastructure during a working visit to the Karaganda region. He instructed the Ministry of Industry and Construction and local authorities to intensify renovation efforts, particularly focusing on road quality and airport modernization.

item.title: Head of Karachaganak Support Service sentenced for fraud totaling 948 million tenge
item.description: Barlyk Mendy gaziev, head of Karachaganak Support Service (KSS), has been found guilty of large-scale fraud by the Uralsk City Court. He was sentenced to eight years in prison, with his total sentence now 10 years, and ordered to pay restitution for the stolen funds.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Denies Reports of Passport-Free Travel Within Turkic States by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has refuted claims circulating online about passport-free travel for citizens of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) starting January 1, 2027. The ministry stated there is no consensus among member states to implement this initiative, and specific timelines for any potential simplification of travel documents have not been determined.

item.title: Former Deputy Interior Minister Reorganizes Profitable Real Estate Fund
item.description: Former Kazakh Deputy Interior Minister Vasily Simachev and other shareholders are reorganizing the 'Alba' real estate investment fund from a joint-stock company to a limited liability partnership. The fund reported a profit of 215 million tenge in 2025, with rental income increasing to 182.4 million tenge.

item.title: CPC Pipeline Tengiz-Novorossiysk Resumes Operations After Scheduled Maintenance
item.description: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) pipeline from Tengiz to Novorossiysk resumed operations on October 6 after a 12-hour scheduled shutdown. During the maintenance, specialists performed technical servicing, repaired defects in Kazakhstan, and conducted upgrades on facilities in Russia and the maritime terminal. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy considers these planned stops when scheduling oil transportation.

item.title: Estonia secures EU sanctions exemption for Russian rare metals supplier
item.description: Estonia has successfully lobbied for the exclusion of a Russian rare metals supplier and an associated individual from the EU's 22nd sanctions package. This exemption is due to Europe's industrial dependence on the strategic raw materials supplied by the company to NPM Silmet.

item.title: Documentary on Afghan Activist Zarqa Yaftali Wins Silver Dolphin at Cannes Awards
item.description: A documentary about Afghan education and women's rights activist Zarqa Yaftali has won the Silver Dolphin award at the 2026 Cannes Media and Television Awards. The film, "Educating Hope in Afghanistan: The Story of Zarqa," highlights her work supporting girls' education and women's rights amid Taliban restrictions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Public Debt Surpasses $10 Billion Amid Rising Repayment Costs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's public debt reached $10.16 billion by the end of July 2026. The government anticipates spending approximately $1.83 billion on external debt servicing between 2027 and 2029. External debt stood at $5.19 billion, with domestic debt at $4.96 billion. The total debt represents about 38% of the projected 2026 GDP.

item.title: Aquatherm Tashkent 2026: Turkish Company Expands Presence in Uzbekistan Market
item.description: The Turkish company Ayvaz is expanding its operations in Uzbekistan, participating in the Aquatherm Tashkent 2026 exhibition. The company, founded in 1948, offers products like compensators and fire safety equipment. Ayvaz recently opened a new representative office, 'Yuroturk,' in Tashkent to foster business contacts and partnerships.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise 10th-11th Grade Curriculum Following Textbook Scandal
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to revise its 10th and 11th-grade school programs, including the literature list, after a scandal erupted over a Russian language and literature textbook. The textbook contained an explicit scene involving Sultan Baibars and a young girl, drawing public outrage. The curriculum review follows an expert evaluation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Adopts Declaration for Human Oversight of Artificial Intelligence in the Workplace
item.description: Kazakhstan's government, employers, and trade unions signed a declaration in Astana calling for human oversight of AI decisions affecting workers' rights. The declaration, adopted at the 'Digital Labor and Artificial Intelligence' forum, emphasizes employer accountability and the right for workers to challenge AI-driven decisions. Kazakhstan's existing AI legislation and Digital Code also provide for transparency and human review of automated decisions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise Clinic Evaluation System, Prioritizing Patient Feedback
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health announced a revised clinic evaluation system that will incorporate patient feedback. The new system will assess factors like wait times for specialist appointments, timely diagnostic tests, and post-discharge follow-up. A 100-point unified system will be implemented, with data automatically calculated quarterly based on information from healthcare information systems.

item.title: Hundreds of Turkmen Citizens Fighting in Ukraine for Russian Army; Ukrainian Officials in Talks with Turkmen Side
item.description: Hundreds of Turkmen citizens are fighting in the Russian army in Ukraine, with reports indicating an increase in recruitment due to severe unemployment and labor migration in Turkmenistan. Ukrainian officials are reportedly in talks with the Turkmen side regarding these fighters, with at least 61 confirmed deaths among them.

item.title: South Korea Recalls Ambassador to Ukraine Amid Tensions After North Korea's Disclosure
item.description: South Korea has recalled its ambassador to Ukraine following tensions that arose after North Korea disclosed the dispatch of its soldiers to Seoul. Despite Ukraine officially apologizing, Seoul was not satisfied and took a strong measure. The situation escalated after North Korea revealed its soldiers were sent to Seoul, prompting South Korea to demand an apology from Kyiv.

item.title: Turkmen Soldiers' Families Report Poor Conditions, Demand Daily Payments for Food
item.description: Families of conscripted soldiers in Turkmenistan report dire conditions in military units, citing poor sanitation, inadequate food, and water shortages. Parents claim they must send 50-150 manats daily to ensure their sons receive sufficient food. Soldiers reportedly suffer from skin diseases due to unsanitary living conditions.

item.title: Tajikistan to Host Central Asia-USA Business Forum in April 2027
item.description: Tajikistan is preparing to host the third Central Asia-USA Business Forum (B5+1) in Dushanbe in April 2027. A preliminary event was held in Washington on October 7th, attended by officials and business representatives. The forum aims to strengthen economic and investment cooperation, focusing on areas like AI, IT, fintech, e-commerce, and strategic minerals.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Public Trust in AI for Healthcare: A Mixed Picture
item.description: A STADA Health Report 2026 study reveals 55% of Uzbekistan's population uses AI for health-related matters, with 69% among those under 35. While AI is seen as a supplementary tool, not a doctor replacement, 47% are hesitant to trust AI diagnoses as much as medical professionals'. A presentation in Tashkent discussed these findings.

item.title: Taliban Interference in Zabul Aid Distribution Diverts Resources from Needy
item.description: Residents of Zabul province report that the Taliban are interfering with humanitarian aid distribution, channeling it to relatives and affiliates. Aid workers coordinate with the group out of fear, leading to aid reaching ineligible individuals. Sources claim only half the aid reaches the intended recipients.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host SCO Transport and Logistics International Exhibition
item.description: An international exhibition titled 'SCO Transport and Logistics' will be held in Dushanbe from October 19-20, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The event aims to showcase member states' potential in transport and logistics, foster business partnerships, and discuss seamless logistical routes within the SCO space.

item.title: Afghan Asylum Seekers in India Face Prolonged Delays, Limited Support
item.description: Afghan women seeking asylum in India report years-long delays in case processing, leaving their futures uncertain. Lack of residency and work permits hinders employment and living expenses. Reduced aid since 2024 and difficulties accessing healthcare exacerbate their situation, impacting children's education.

item.title: WHO Does Not Confirm New Illness Cases in Irkutsk Region
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) has not confirmed new illness cases among individuals who contacted an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute diagnosed with pneumonia. Rospotrebnadzor stated that the WHO has no confirmed information on new cases and has received full details on measures taken, confirming no public health risks.

item.title: UN Mission Reports Over 50 Women Detained by Taliban for Dress Code Violations
item.description: The UN mission in Afghanistan reported that Taliban authorities detained at least 52 women and one girl in Kabul and Herat over three months for alleged dress code violations. Reasons included visible hair, colorful scarves, or appearing in public without a male guardian. UNAMA expressed grave concern, stating these acts violate women's rights and could lead to social stigma.
